PullRequest.Title: canvases: offer user, workspace, and plugin creation scopes
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

- Have `/create-canvas` offer user, workspace, and plugin scope before creating files, unless the user already specified a scope.
- Carry the selected location through implementation and validation, including plugin manifest and loading requirements and cross-workspace resource handling.
- Extend the built-in skill contract tests to cover scope selection while preserving the host-neutral authoring contract. No runtime behavior changes.

## Validation

- `npm --prefix extensions/copilot run test:unit -- src/platform/promptFiles/test/node/builtinSkills.spec.ts` — passed, all 3 tests; rerun after updating to current main.
- `npm --prefix extensions/copilot run lint-staged -- src/platform/promptFiles/test/node/builtinSkills.spec.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --cached --check` — passed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start a Copilot CLI session with canvases enabled and discover the create-canvas skill
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session creation calls getSkillsLocations alongside agent discovery, and the skill registry exposes the skill name, description, and URI. The enlarged SKILL.md body is not injected into every session; detailed instructions are loaded only when the skill is selected, so the changed body is off the normal session-start critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Obtain registered skills through vscode.chat.getSkills for CLI session options and customization discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One registry request per existing discovery call, covering all skills; this diff adds no skill and no additional call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same create-canvas skill contribution was enumerated at the same URI and under the same canvases feature condition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing request is on CLI session/customization discovery, but the changed SKILL.md body does not add another request or cause full-body processing in the shown consumers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read skill metadata/body as managed by the host skill registry and later load the detailed SKILL.md when invoked.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing skill file; full-body load is on skill invocation rather than multiplied by workspace items or canvases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SKILL.md was already registered and loaded; only its constant-size content changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The body is relevant only to create-canvas execution; the modest constant size increase does not create a realistic I/O or serialization regression.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of enabled skills, unchanged by this diff; this PR modifies one existing skill and changes its short description by only a small constant amount.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Agent and skill discovery run concurrently via Promise.all; skill enumeration itself remains one registry request with no new per-skill operation introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Skill registration, enablement, and registry lookup behavior are unchanged. The same URI and contribution key are used, so no new cache key, miss path, or invalidation behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that startup/discovery cardinality is unchanged based on the manifest contribution, getSkills wrapper, and CLI session call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The host registry's internal metadata caching is outside the repository context, but the unchanged URI, contribution count, and consumer call cardinality establish that the diff does not add a scaling mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: one existing skill remains one registry entry, and the larger instructions are not added as repeated per-message or per-item work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke /create-canvas without specifying a scope and create a user- or workspace-scoped canvas
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The invoked skill now waits for one ask_user response before writing when scope is unspecified, then inspects one selected location, writes one extension, checks it, reloads providers once, and performs the existing runtime validation sequence. The user interaction is intentionally required to preserve the newly offered scope semantics, not accidental repeated work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ask the user to choose among user, workspace, and plugin scopes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one prompt per create-canvas invocation when the user did not already specify scope; zero when scope is explicit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The workflow immediately selected workspace scope and did not ask this question.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks file creation until the user chooses, as required to avoid inferring workspace scope.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Inspect extension conventions and create extension.mjs in the selected extension directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected directory and one extension tree; the instructions explicitly prohibit copies at other scopes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same inspection and extension creation occurred in the workspace .github/extensions directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required implementation work remains on the creation path and is not fanned out across all three offered scopes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run node --check for the generated extension.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One syntax check per created extension.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior instructions also required one node --check invocation for the workspace extension.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains on validation before success is reported.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload extension providers and call list_canvas_capabilities, open_canvas, optional invoke_canvas_action, then reopen the same instance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One global reload plus a constant validation sequence for the single generated canvas; action validation occurs only when actions exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior workflow already required the same reload and runtime validation sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains required before reporting success; no new per-workspace or per-scope loop is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One canvas creation request and one selected scope; workspace count and number of available scopes do not multiply file creation because the prompt explicitly forbids copies at other scopes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The workflow is intentionally sequential because scope selection determines the only destination. Validation operations are ordered around one provider reload; no aggregate concurrency burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is added or bypassed. The selected location is resolved once per creation; warm/cold provider behavior after reload is unchanged from the prior workspace flow.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the one-question critical path and single-destination invariant from the changed prompt text.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual time waiting for a user choice varies and provider reload duration depends on installed providers, but neither cost scales with scope count or collection size under the changed instructions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: the only new blocking step is one intentional choice required by the feature, while all expensive implementation and validation work remains bounded to one selected destination.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or update a plugin-scoped canvas and validate that the host can discover it
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After plugin scope is selected, the workflow resolves one plugin source, writes or preserves one manifest, creates one extension, ensures that source is installed or loaded once, then executes the same provider reload and runtime checks. Plugin loading is necessary for discoverability and is not repeated per workspace.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Inspect one plugin source and create or update .plugin/plugin.json plus one extension directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected plugin manifest and one canvas extension per invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Plugin scope did not exist; the prior path wrote one extension under the workspace and no plugin manifest.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before plugin discovery; new compared with workspace-only creation but constant and scope-specific.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install or load the selected plugin from source using the host-supported workflow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one plugin-source load/install for the chosen plugin per creation flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The workspace extension did not require a plugin installation/loading step.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for the host to discover the newly created plugin canvas; the prompt does not direct loading multiple plugins or workspaces.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload all extension providers after the plugin source is available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One reload per create/modify workflow, unchanged from the previous validation contract.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Workspace extension creation already called extensions_reload once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider restart remains on the validation path; plugin creation broadens where the extension may originate but does not increase reload count.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate discovery and behavior with list/open/action/reopen canvas calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A constant sequence against the one generated canvas.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior workspace flow used the same runtime checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for success confirmation and unchanged in multiplicity.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One chosen plugin and one generated canvas extension. Existing plugin metadata/components may affect manifest size, but the instruction requires preservation rather than copying or traversing every installed plugin.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Plugin source selection, manifest update, load/install, reload, and runtime checks are serialized by their dependencies. No Promise.all-style unbounded installation or provider creation is directed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Installed-cache mutation is explicitly avoided as the workflow operates in plugin source. Host plugin installation/loading caches are not specified, but the directive performs one supported workflow per creation and does not add retries or duplicate installs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that plugin-only extra work is constant-cardinality and sequential from the explicit prompt contract; exact host implementation cost is unknown.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The supported plugin workflow could involve host-specific filesystem or network activity not defined by this repository, but the changed contract bounds it to one selected plugin and requires it for functional discoverability.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: plugin scope necessarily adds one manifest and one load/install operation, with no collection fan-out, retry loop, cache defeat, or concurrency burst.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the built-in skill contract unit test
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test synchronously reads package.json once in one test and SKILL.md once in the contract test, then scans a fixed list of required substrings and several negative patterns. The added anchors modestly increase constant test-only CPU work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read SKILL.md synchronously for contract assertions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per contract-test execution, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same test already performed one synchronous read of the same file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only blocks this unit test, not product startup or canvas execution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One parse in the contribution test, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Test-only and unaffected by the changed contract assertions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One package manifest, one skill file, and a fixed required-anchor array growing from the prior list by ten constant entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Vitest scheduling is outside this test, while operations inside the test are synchronous and unchanged in structure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No explicit cache exists in the test; each test run reads the same two local files as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete test diff and surrounding test body.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact micro-cost of additional includes checks is not measured, but input and assertion counts are tiny and fixed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: added fixed-string assertions create negligible constant test-only work and no realistic scaling path.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced skill discovery, invocation, user/workspace creation, plugin creation, validation, and test execution. The PR introduces one intentional scope-selection interaction and bounded plugin-only setup, but no repeated expensive work, boundary fan-out, eager product-path initialization, cache lifecycle regression, unbounded retention, serialization amplification, or concurrency burst.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
